guide.title: Git Workflow Guide
guide.description: Learn the essential Git commands and workflows for effective version control

daily.title: Daily Workflow
daily.description: Basic steps for everyday Git work

step1.title: 1. Check your current branch
step1.description: Always verify which branch you're on with 'git branch' or check the status bar. This helps avoid accidental work on the wrong branch.

step2.title: 2. Update your local repository
step2.description: Run 'git fetch' to download the latest changes from remote without modifying your working directory.

step3.title: 3. Integrate remote changes
step3.description: Run 'git pull' to fetch AND merge changes from the remote into your current branch before starting new work.

step5.title: 5. Stage your changes
step5.description: Use 'git add <files>' or 'git add .' to stage your changes for committing.

step6.title: 6. Commit your changes
step6.description: Use 'git commit -m "Your descriptive message"' to save your staged changes locally.

step7.title: 7. Push your changes
step7.description: Use 'git push' to upload your local commits to the remote repository.

step1.title: 1. Create a new branch
step1.description: Use 'git branch <branch-name>' to create a branch (without switching to it).

step2.title: 2. Create and switch to a new branch
step2.description: Use 'git checkout -b <branch-name>' to create a branch and immediately switch to it.

step3.title: 3. Switch between branches
step3.description: Use 'git checkout <branch-name>' to switch to an existing branch.

step4.title: 4. List all branches
step4.description: Use 'git branch' to see all local branches. The current branch will be marked with an asterisk (*).

step5.title: 5. Get remote branches
step5.description: Use 'git fetch' to update remote branch information, then 'git branch -r' to see remote branches.

merging.title: Merging Workflow
merging.description: How to merge changes between branches

step1.title: 1. Switch to the target branch
step1.description: First use 'git checkout <target-branch>' to switch to the branch you want to merge INTO. This is critical - you must be ON the receiving branch.

step2.title: 2. Update the target branch
step2.description: Run 'git pull' to make sure your target branch is up to date with the remote.

step3.title: 3. Merge the source branch
step3.description: Use 'git merge <source-branch>' to merge changes FROM the source branch INTO your current (target) branch.

step4.title: 4. Resolve any conflicts
step4.description: If there are merge conflicts, Git will notify you. Edit the conflicted files, then 'git add' them once resolved.

step5.title: 5. Resolving Merge Conflicts (In Detail)
step5.description: When conflicts occur, Git marks them in files with special markers. Open each conflicted file and look for sections with '<<<<<<< HEAD', '=======', and '>>>>>>> branch-name'. The content between '<<<<<<< HEAD' and '=======' is from your current branch, while content between '=======' and '>>>>>>> branch-name' is from the branch being merged. Edit these sections to create the final version, removing all conflict markers. After resolving, run 'git add <file>' on each fixed file and commit with 'git commit'.

step6.title: 6. Complete the merge
step6.description: If there were conflicts, use 'git commit' to finalize the merge. Otherwise, the merge is completed automatically.

step7.title: 7. Push the merged changes
step7.description: Use 'git push' to upload the merged changes to the remote repository.

step1.title: Discard local changes
step1.description: Use 'git reset --hard' to discard all local changes and reset to the last commit.

step2.title: Discard all unstaged changes
step2.description: Use 'git checkout -- .' to discard all unstaged changes in your working directory. This is safer than reset --hard as it only affects unstaged changes.

step3.title: Discard changes for specific file
step3.description: Use 'git checkout -- <file>' to discard changes to a specific file and restore it to the version in HEAD.

step4.title: Unstage files
step4.description: Use 'git reset HEAD <file>' to unstage a file while keeping your changes.

step5.title: Fix last commit message
step5.description: Use 'git commit --amend' to modify your most recent commit message (before pushing).

step6.title: Undo last commit
step6.description: Use 'git reset HEAD~1' to undo the last commit but keep the changes staged.

step7.title: Check commit history
step7.description: Use 'git log' to see the commit history and find specific commits if needed.

step8.title: Abort a merge with conflicts
step8.description: If you've started a merge but want to cancel it due to too many conflicts, use 'git merge --abort' to return to the state before the merge started.

explanations.gitFetch: In a real Git repository, this command would download objects and refs from a remote repository. It updates your remote-tracking branches without modifying your working directory or local branches.
explanations.gitPull: In a real Git repository, this command would fetch from and integrate with another repository or a local branch. It combines git fetch and git merge in one step.
explanations.gitPush: In a real Git repository, this command would update remote refs along with associated objects, sending your local branch commits to the remote repository branch.
explanations.simulationFetch: This is a simulation: In real Git, fetch would download commits, files, and refs from a remote repository.
explanations.simulationPull: This is a simulation: In real Git, pull would fetch and merge remote changes into your current branch.
explanations.simulationPush: This is a simulation: In real Git, push would upload your branch commits to the remote repository.

gitCommands.fetch: Fetch latest changes from the remote repository
gitCommands.pull: Fetch and merge changes from the remote repository
gitCommands.push: Push local changes to the remote repository

howToUse.title: How to Use This Git Playground
howToUse.subtitle: Follow these steps to learn Git concepts visually.
howToUse.switchBranchDesc: Use the 'Branches' section in 'Git Controls' (bottom panel) to switch to an existing branch or create a new one. Your file modifications and new commits will apply to this active branch.
howToUse.editCodeDesc: Modify the code in the 'Code Editor' on the left.
howToUse.stageChangesDesc: Once you've made changes, click 'Git Add (Stage Changes)' in 'Git Controls'. This prepares your modifications for the next commit on the active branch.
howToUse.commitChangesDesc: Enter a commit message and click 'Git Commit'. This saves a snapshot of your staged changes on the current active branch. The Git Graph will update.
howToUse.createBranchDesc: In 'Git Controls', type a new branch name under the 'Branches' section and click 'Create'. This creates a new branch from the current commit (HEAD).
howToUse.mergeBranchesDesc1: In 'Git Controls', under 'Merge Branches', select the branch you want to merge from (source) and the branch you want to merge into (target).
howToUse.mergeBranchesDesc2: Click 'Merge Branches'. A new merge commit will be created on the target branch, and the graph will update. The target branch becomes active.
howToUse.viewHistoryDesc: The 'Git Graph' (middle panel) visualizes your commit history. Click on any commit node in the graph to see its details and content in the right panel.
howToUse.viewChangesDesc: When you stage changes using 'Git Add', a diff view will automatically appear in the right panel showing the differences between your changes and the HEAD commit.
howToUse.experimentDesc: Try different sequences of commands to see how the Git history and file states change!
